rationale:
The three artifacts describe one pre-existing defect in LinkedLruHashMap.removeLru. The buggy parent revision ee39eb4 executes `_tail = _tail.previous; _tail.next = null;`, so when the map drops to zero entries the tail becomes null (NPE/failed unlink) and `_head` is left dangling at the evicted node. The fix in lib/src/collection/lru_map.dart makes the tail write null-aware and clears `_head` when the list empties, matching the commit/PR record 'Correct putIfAbsent when maximumSize is 1 (#480) -- If we remove the last element in the map in removeLru, we need to clear out _head as well.' The trigger 'handles maximumSize 1 correctly' sets maximumSize = 1, calls putIfAbsent('B', ...), and asserts keys == ['B'], which is exactly the eviction-to-empty path that leaves a stale head, and it uses only pre-existing public API (maximumSize setter, putIfAbsent, keys); the fix introduces no new API. The minimized production patch equals the production half of the single upstream commit: five lines in one method, with only an explanatory comment attached to the new branch, no reformatting, no feature extension, no config or doc-only edits. The test half is separated into patches/trigger-tests.patch and is byte-identical to the upstream test hunk, so the trigger is upstream-native rather than curator-authored. active_same_project_root_causes is empty and google/quiver-dart#480 is the sole entry in allowed_root_cause_ids, so no duplicate root cause. Runtime gates are taken only from the supplied strict evidence: both strict_original and strict_post_minimization report passed=true with no failed checks, including buggy differential reproduction of the single declared selector, deterministic fingerprints across 3 repetitions, fixed isolated/suite/reversed runs clean, and fixed full suite all green.

The defect is a pre-existing null/state-consistency bug in LinkedLruHashMap.removeLru: after `_tail = _tail.previous`, the code unconditionally wrote `_tail.next = null`, which breaks when the map drops to zero entries, and `_head` was left pointing at the evicted node. The production patch changes exactly that: `_tail?.next = null` plus clearing `_head` when `_tail == null` (patches/minimized-production.patch, lib/src/collection/lru_map.dart, single hunk of 1 removed / 6 added lines). The commit subject and body ('Correct putIfAbsent when maximumSize is 1 (#480)' / 'If we remove the last element in the map in removeLru, we need to clear out _head as well') describe the same failure mode, and traceability.verified_fix_issue_numbers resolves to 480, which matches the sole allowed root cause id. The trigger is the unchanged upstream test from the same fixing commit ('handles maximumSize 1 correctly'): it sets maximumSize = 1, calls putIfAbsent, and asserts keys == ['B'] — all pre-existing public API on LruMap, with no API introduced by the fix, so it is semantically equivalent to the reported defect rather than a feature probe. The minimized patch is production-only with no formatting, doc, config, or test churn; the test edit lives solely in patches/trigger-tests.patch. Machine-generated strict gates pass in both the original and post-minimization runs: trigger.buggy_differential reproduces the declared selector alone, trigger.fixed_clean is green across isolated/suite/reversed runs, trigger.deterministic shows 3/3 fingerprint groups, full_suite.buggy_reproduces_only_triggers confirms no collateral failures, and build.both_versions passes. active_same_project_root_causes is empty, so this root cause duplicates no registry entry.
